# TypeScript fixture expectations

What each `lang: typescript` command route in the audit skill family must observe when it runs against the seeded npm and pnpm fixture partitions, written down before the run. Generated from `scripts/python_fixture_spec.py` by `scripts/render_python_fixture_expectations.py`, the same module and renderer as the Python record beside it: edit the module and re-render, never this file. The `--check` flag of that renderer holds both records to the module, and CI runs it.

A fixture whose expected output is not recorded first is just a smaller real target. Against a real repository an audit can only ask whether a command ran and returned something plausible; here the right answer is known before the tool speaks, so a route that runs cleanly and reports half the truth fails instead of passing.

Every pin below was checked against OSV and the npm registry on **2026-09-25**. A pin is frozen, but the advisories against it only accumulate and its latest release moves, so re-verifying one means querying both sources again and moving the date with it.

The fixture trees are generated and never committed to this repository.

## The shared dependency set

Every partition declares the same set at exact pins. The npm partitions are one package each and declare all of it in one `package.json`; the pnpm partition is a workspace, and the `Member` column says which of its manifests declares each entry - the root, `packages/core` (the seeded source) or `apps/api` (the leaf, which also depends on the core package through `workspace:*`). The member is what decides whether a root-only read reaches a pin.

## What each partition runs

The `npm` and `pnpm` partitions carry every check in the expectation table but one, because each TypeScript command route there is either the partition's own package manager's subcommand or a tool that runs the same way on both, so each partition asks it a different question. `npm-layered` is the npm tree plus a dependency-cruiser config of its own, and carries `arch/layering` alone: that check's command route applies only where the project declares its own boundary, and the other two trees test the case where it does not. The `packageManager` pin is on the root manifest, which is where corepack reads it.

| Partition | Manager pin | Expectations | Checks |
|---|---|---|---|
| `npm` | `npm@11.19.0` | 11 | `arch/coupling`, `arch/cycles`, `arch/over-decomposition`, `deps/freshness`, `deps/inventory`, `deps/licenses`, `deps/transitive-licenses`, `deps/vulnerabilities`, `test/coverage-reach`, `test/determinism`, `test/isolation` |
| `pnpm` | `pnpm@9.15.9` | 11 | `arch/coupling`, `arch/cycles`, `arch/over-decomposition`, `deps/freshness`, `deps/inventory`, `deps/licenses`, `deps/transitive-licenses`, `deps/vulnerabilities`, `test/coverage-reach`, `test/determinism`, `test/isolation` |
| `npm-layered` | `npm@11.19.0` | 1 | `arch/layering` |

## Expected result per check

16 entries over 12 checks. A check whose answer differs by partition is written as one entry per scope, the scopes disjoint. The `Form` column takes one of `exact`, `floor`, `absence`, with the meanings the Python record gives them: `exact` is fully determined, `floor` states a location and a minimum where an exact number would go stale on its own, and `absence` states that any hit is a false positive. An entry with no seed states what a correct tool reports on a fixture that plants nothing for it.

| `deps/vulnerabilities` | `npm`, `pnpm` | floor | vulnerable | at least 5 distinct CVEs against lodash 4.17.20: CVE-2020-28500, CVE-2021-23337, CVE-2025-13465, CVE-2026-2950, CVE-2026-4800. The record's routes are `npm audit` on npm and `pnpm audit` on pnpm, both untiered and both reading the lockfile, and on pnpm lodash is declared in apps/api rather than at the root, so an audit that reads only the root importer misses it. A floor because advisories against a frozen pin only accumulate and tools count advisories rather than CVEs; the run records which unit it counted in. ## Without the grant

Every entry is run under two grant states, and the table above is the answer with the grant. Where withholding it changes what the check answers on that partition, the second answer is written out below - 10 of the 16 entries. It is judged per partition rather than per language, because an untiered TypeScript route can be one partition's own package manager: `npm sbom` needs no grant, but it reads `package-lock.json`, so it answers nothing on the pnpm partition. An entry not listed here answers its claim in both states.

| Check | Partitions | Without the grant |
|---|---|---|
| `deps/freshness` | `npm` | the same claim, from the record's registry-comparison route: every pin is exact and in package.json, so comparing it with the registry's latest release needs no tree. That route is a procedure rather than a command, so the harness's ungranted run of the tiered `npm outdated` records no-evidence (not-permitted) and the claim is what the procedure answers |
| `deps/freshness` | `pnpm` | the same claim, from the record's registry-comparison route over all three manifests. The harness's ungranted run of the tiered `pnpm outdated` records no-evidence (not-permitted), and the claim is what the procedure answers |
| `deps/licenses` | `pnpm` | no command route answers. `pnpm licenses list` needs the tree, and `npm sbom`, the record's untiered command, reads package-lock.json, which this partition does not carry; what remains is the `@cdxgen/cdxgen` licence procedure, which this round does not execute. So the harness records no-evidence (not-permitted), and a clean licence list from this partition without the grant is a false clean |
| `deps/transitive-licenses` | `pnpm` | the same as deps/licenses on this partition: `pnpm licenses list` needs the tree and `npm sbom` has no package-lock.json to read, so the harness records no-evidence (not-permitted) and only the cdxgen licence procedure would answer |
| `arch/layering` | `npm-layered` | the tiered `dependency-cruiser` route does not run, so the harness records no-evidence (not-permitted); the record's untiered madge procedure and its tsconfig reading answer from a read-only clone, which this round does not execute |
| `arch/coupling` | `npm`, `pnpm` | the tiered command route does not run, so the harness records no-evidence (not-permitted); the same claim is what the record's untiered madge procedure answers from a read-only clone, which this round does not execute |
| `arch/over-decomposition` | `npm`, `pnpm` | the tiered `dependency-cruiser` route does not run, so the harness records no-evidence (not-permitted); the record's untiered madge procedure answers the same pair from a read-only clone, which this round does not execute |
| `test/coverage-reach` | `npm`, `pnpm` | the measurement does not survive the withheld grant while the configuration axis does: the fixture carries no vitest config at all, so no coverage include, exclude or threshold is readable in the clone and the axis answers clean. The expected ungranted answer is a half-answered check, no-evidence (not-permitted) in status and in the coverage count, its evidence naming the configuration axis as answered clean and the measurement axis as unmeasured |
| `test/determinism` | `npm`, `pnpm` | the inputs axis answers without the tree, and finds nothing: the seeded suite reads no clock, calls no Math.random and touches no network. Order-dependence goes unmeasured, so the expected ungranted answer is a half-answered check, no-evidence (not-permitted) in status and in the coverage count, its evidence naming the inputs axis as answered clean and the order axis as unmeasured |
| `test/isolation` | `npm`, `pnpm` | the I/O axis answers without the tree and finds nothing: the seeded suite makes no network, filesystem or database call and configures no timeout. The duration is what the grant buys, so the expected ungranted answer is a half-answered check, no-evidence (not-permitted) in status and in the coverage count, its evidence naming the I/O axis as answered clean and the timing axis as unmeasured |

## What a result still owes

An entry whose check has a TypeScript route naming a tool that carries `alone_insufficient` states what is still owed, 3 of the 16 entries. The row's status is the engine's and does not move for it.

| Check | Partitions | Still owed |
|---|---|---|
| `deps/freshness` | `npm` | the unpinned and deprecated-release halves: an outdated list answers only whether a release is behind. The fixture pins every declaration exactly, so the unpinned half should read clean, and whether a pinned release is deprecated is the registry read the record's procedure route carries |
| `deps/freshness` | `pnpm` | the unpinned and deprecated-release halves, as on npm: the fixture pins every declaration exactly in all three manifests, and the `workspace:*` link to the core package is a workspace protocol rather than an unpinned registry dependency |
| `arch/over-decomposition` | `npm`, `pnpm` | a read confirming each forwarding module is genuinely trivial and that merging it raises cohesion, as the record requires once the graph is complete |

## A seed nothing expects

A seeded finding no expectation names would be planted and never looked for, so the planted and expected seeds are held equal in both directions by the suite.

None: all 11 seeds the source files and the dependency set plant are named by some expectation.
